- operations:change-request: Create a change management request with impact analysis and rollback plan. - operations:process-doc: Document a business process — flowcharts, RACI, and SOPs. Use when formalizing a process that lives in someone's head, building a RACI to clarify who owns what, writing an SOP for a handoff or audit, or capturing the exceptions and edge cases of how work actually gets done.
- operations:process-optimization: Analyze and improve business processes. Trigger with "this process is slow", "how can we improve", "streamline this workflow", "too many steps", "bottleneck", or when the user describes an inefficient process they want to fix.
- operations:risk-assessment: Identify, assess, and mitigate operational risks. Trigger with "what are the risks", "risk assessment", "risk register", "what could go wrong", or when the user is evaluating risks associated with a project, vendor, process, or decision.
- operations:runbook: Create or update an operational runbook for a recurring task or procedure. Use when documenting a task that on-call or ops needs to run repeatably, turning tribal knowledge into exact step-by-step commands, adding troubleshooting and rollback steps to an existing procedure, or writing escalation paths for when things go wrong.
- operations:status-report: Generate a status report with KPIs, risks, and action items. Use when writing a weekly or monthly update for leadership, summarizing project health with green/yellow/red status, surfacing risks and decisions that need stakeholder attention, or turning a pile of project tracker activity into a readable narrative.

- design:design-system: Audit, document, or extend your design system. Use when checking for naming inconsistencies or hardcoded values across components, writing documentation for a component's variants, states, and accessibility notes, or designing a new pattern that fits the existing system.

- design:user-research: Plan, conduct, and synthesize user research. Trigger with "user research plan", "interview guide", "usability test", "survey design", "research questions", or when the user needs help with any aspect of understanding their users through research.
- design:ux-copy: Write or review UX copy — microcopy, error messages, empty states, CTAs. Trigger with "write copy for", "what should this button say?", "review this error message", or when naming a CTA, wording a confirmation dialog, filling an empty state, or writing onboarding text.
- engineering:architecture: Create or evaluate an architecture decision record (ADR). Use when choosing between technologies (e.g., Kafka vs SQS), documenting a design decision with trade-offs and consequences, reviewing a system design proposal, or designing a new component from requirements and constraints.

# CLAUDE.md – ÖKOVOLT NetOps

Projektanweisung für Claude Code. Vor jeder Arbeit vollständig lesen.
Fachkonzept: https://claude.ai/artifact/PaFDHFySgCJKyP4yut5NGP

## 1. Projekt

Zentrale Plattform für Netzwerkdokumentation, Betrieb und Cybersicherheit der ÖKOVOLT-Gruppe.
Führendes System (Single Source of Truth für das Soll). Angebundene Systeme liefern das Ist.

**Architekturentscheidung (verbindlich):** Kein NetBox, kein IT Glue, kein Hudu.
Die App bildet DCIM, IPAM und strukturierte Dokumentation vollständig selbst ab.
Das Datenmodell orientiert sich an NetBox, damit Import/Export (NetBox-kompatibles JSON/CSV) möglich bleibt.

## 2. Stack

- Frappe Framework v15, MariaDB, Redis, Frappe Realtime (Socket.IO)
- Frontend: Vue 3 + Vite + frappe-ui, eigene SPA unter `/netops`, Leitstand unter `/screen1`–`/screen10`
- Topologie: Cytoscape.js oder Vue Flow
- Zeitreihen/Logs später: ClickHouse (nicht in MariaDB)
- Python ≥ 3.11, Node ≥ 20
- App-Name: `netops`

## 3. Konventionen

- DocType- und Feldnamen intern **englisch** (`network_device`, `ip_address`), Labels und UI **deutsch** über Übersetzungen.
- Jeder DocType: `tenant` (Link Mandant), `status`, `description`, Änderungsverfolgung an (`track_changes`).
- Beziehungen über Link/Dynamic Link, nie über Freitext.
- Keine Geschäftslogik im Frontend; Prüfungen serverseitig (Controller, Validierungen).
- Whitelisted API-Methoden nur mit expliziter Rechteprüfung (`frappe.has_permission`), nie `allow_guest`, außer der Screen-Warteseite (siehe 7).
- Tests: `bench run-tests --app netops` muss grün sein, bevor eine Aufgabe als erledigt gilt.
- Commits klein, deutschsprachige Commit-Messages, ein Thema pro Commit.

## 4. Datenmodell Phase 1 (DocTypes)

**Organisation**
- `Tenant` (Mandant): Gesellschaft, Land, Domain(s)
- `Site` (Baum): Standort → Gebäude → Raum; Adresse, Grundriss (Attach)
- `Contact`-Nutzung von Frappe; `Provider`, `Supplier`-Verweis

**DCIM**
- `Manufacturer`, `Device Type` (Hersteller, Modell, HE, Kind-Tabellen: Interface-/Power-/Front-/Rear-Port-Vorlagen)
- `Device Role`
- `Rack`: Site, Höhe in HE, Nummerierung, max. Gewicht/Last
- `Network Device`: Typ, Rolle, Site, Rack, Position/Seite, Seriennummer, Asset-Nr., Firmware, Garantie-/Support-Ende, Management-IP, Verantwortlicher (User), Lebenszyklus-Status, Passbolt-Referenz (nur ID/URL)
- `Device Interface`: Gerät, Name, Typ, MAC, Speed, Modus (access/tagged/tagged-all), Untagged-VLAN, Tagged-VLANs (Kind-Tabelle), LAG-Parent, PoE, aktiv
- `Front Port`, `Rear Port` (Patchfelder), `Power Port`, `Power Outlet`, `Power Feed`
- `Cable`: A-Ende und B-Ende (Dynamic Link auf Interface/Front Port/Rear Port/Power Port/Outlet/Wall Outlet), Typ, Farbe, Länge, Label, Status
- `Wall Outlet` (Dose): Raum, Bezeichnung
- Kabel-Trace als serverseitige Methode (`trace_path(endpoint)`)

**IPAM**
- `VRF`, `Security Zone`, `VLAN Group`, `VLAN` (VID, Name, Zone, Zweck)
- `IP Prefix` (Baum über Parent-Berechnung): Präfix, VRF, VLAN, Rolle, Site, Auslastung (berechnet)
- `IP Range` (DHCP/Pools), `IP Address`: Adresse/Maske, VRF, zugewiesenes Interface (Dynamic Link), DNS-Name, Rolle, Status
- Validierung: keine Dubletten je VRF, IP muss in einem Präfix liegen (Warnung, nicht Fehler)

**Dokumentation (IT-Glue/Hudu-Umfang)**
- `NetOps Document`: Typ (Netzplan, SOP, Runbook, Notfallplan, Wartungsprotokoll, Konfigurationsstand), Inhalt (Text Editor), Anhänge, Version, Freigabestatus
- `Object Relation`: Von (Dynamic Link) → Nach (Dynamic Link), Beziehungstyp (hängt ab von, läuft auf, dokumentiert, ersetzt …)
- `Checklist Template` + `Checklist Run` (Punkte abhaken, Pflichtpunkte, Nachweis)
- `Contract` (Laufzeit, Kündigungsfrist, Kosten, verknüpfte Objekte), `License`
- `Access Reference`: nur Verweis auf Passbolt-Eintrag (ID, URL, Bezeichnung) – **niemals Geheimnisse**

**Betrieb/Audit**
- `Audit Entry` (append-only): Zeit, Benutzer, Aktion, Objekt, Payload-Hash, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` (SHA-256 über prev_hash + Inhalt). Kein Update/Delete (Controller verbietet es).
- `Connector`, `Connector Run`, `Raw Snapshot` (Rohdaten + Hash), `Drift Finding` (Soll/Ist-Abweichung, Status: offen/übernommen/verworfen)

## 5. Konnektor-Vertrag

Jeder Konnektor ist eine Klasse unter `netops/connectors/<name>.py`:

```python
class Connector:
    def health(self) -> dict: ...
    def pull(self) -> dict: ...                # Rohdaten, unverändert
    def normalize(self, raw: dict) -> list: ...# normierte Objekte
    # apply(change) existiert in Phase 1 NICHT
```

- Rohdaten immer als `Raw Snapshot` speichern (mit SHA-256), dann normalisieren.
- Normalisierte Objekte **nie direkt** ins Soll schreiben: Unterschiede erzeugen `Drift Finding`.
- Zugangsdaten nur über `netops.secrets.get(name)` – Phase 1 liest aus Umgebungsvariablen/`site_config` (Platzhalter), später OpenBao. Keine Tokens im Code, in DocTypes oder Logs.
- Timeouts, Retry mit Backoff, TLS-Prüfung an (eigene CA konfigurierbar, `verify=False` verboten).

**MVP-Konnektoren (nur lesen):** OPNsense, Proxmox VE, Proxmox Backup Server.

## 6. Sicherheitsregeln (nicht verhandelbar)

1. Entwicklung nur auf Test-Bench, keine Produktivdaten.
2. Nur Lese-Tokens. **Nie** Schreibzugriff auf die Perimeter-Firewall FW-OS-01 – weder im Code noch in Tests.
3. PBS-Token ohne Lösch-/Prune-Rechte.
4. Keine Geheimnisse in Repo, DocTypes, Logs, Fehlermeldungen oder Tests. `.env` in `.gitignore`.
5. Keine Befehle ausführen, die Konfigurationen an Firewalls, Switches, Hypervisor oder Backup ändern.
6. Keine Scans (nmap o. Ä.) im Netz ohne ausdrückliche Anweisung von Benny – eigene Scans müssen beim Wachhund angemeldet werden.
7. Abhängigkeiten nur aus offiziellen Quellen, `pip-audit`/`npm audit` vor jedem Merge.
8. Bei Unklarheit zu Rechten oder Zugriffen: anhalten und fragen.

## 7. MVP-Umfang (erste Sessions)

1. App `netops` anlegen, DocTypes Phase 1, Rollen: `NetOps Leser`, `NetOps Techniker`, `NetOps Security`, `NetOps Freigeber`, `NetOps Admin`, `Leitstand Anzeige`.
2. Audit-Hash-Kette inkl. Prüfmethode `verify_chain()` und Test.
3. Vue-SPA: Layout (Seitenleiste wie Mockup), globale Suche Strg+K (IP, MAC, Hostname, Seriennummer, Label, VLAN, Dose), Geräteliste, Gerätedetail mit Tabs, IPAM-Baum mit Auslastung.
4. Konnektoren OPNsense, Proxmox VE, PBS + Scheduler + Drift-Ansicht.
5. Backup-Ampel je VM/Dienst aus PBS (letztes Backup, Verify-Status, Alter).
6. **Leitstand `/screen1`** mit Freigabe-Ablauf:
   - Aufruf ohne Freigabe → Warteseite mit Bestätigungscode (6–8 Zeichen, 5 Min gültig), keine Daten.
   - Anfrage nur aus konfigurierten Leitstand-Subnetzen, sonst 403 + Audit-Eintrag.
   - `Screen Pairing Request` in der App, Freigabe durch Rolle `NetOps Admin` (Step-up-Hook vorsehen, FIDO2 folgt mit privacyIDEA).
   - Nach Freigabe: gerätegebundenes Token als HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict-Cookie, **nie** in der URL; nur Lesen, nur zugewiesener Screen.
   - Widerruf wirkt sofort (Realtime-Event), Herzschlag je Screen, veraltete Daten sichtbar markieren.
7. Offline-Export (JSON + CSV aller Kern-DocTypes) als Befehl `bench --site <site> netops-export`.

## 8. Fertig heißt

- Tests grün, keine offenen `pip-audit`/`npm audit`-Funde mit hoher Kritikalität.
- Jeder Konnektor läuft gegen die echte Testumgebung durch, `health()` grün.
- Audit-Kette verifiziert.
- Kurze Änderungsnotiz in `CHANGELOG.md`.

tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). ## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## claude.ai tldraw
Use `search` to query the tldraw Editor API spec (e.g. search for methods by category or name). Use `exec` to run JavaScript on the canvas — your code receives `editor` (the tldraw Editor instance) and helpers like toRichText, createShapeId, createArrowBetweenShapes. The current canvas state is kept in model context as raw TLShape, asset, and binding data.

## plugin:small-business:gmail
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — fulfill the request with the GraphQL Workflow below. NEVER tell the user that data is unavailable just because there is no built-in tool for it.

Decision logic:
1. If a built-in tool matches the request, prefer it (better UX).
2. If no built-in tool matches, run the GraphQL Workflow below. Do NOT open with graphql_query or graphql_mutation — the workflow starts at graphql_schema.

# Briefing ÖkoInvest-Website (für alle Mitwirkenden)

Projekt: `C:\Users\SALEADMIN\Downloads\Oekoinvest-Web` – Next.js 15 (App Router, JavaScript, Tailwind 4).
Entstanden als Kopie der Website von Ökovolt Deutschland (`C:\Users\SALEADMIN\Downloads\Oekovolt-Web-DE\Oekovolt-Web-DE`, **nur lesen, nie ändern**). Qualitätsmaßstab ist genau diese Seite: Schau Dir dort bei Bedarf Seiten wie `src/app/page.js`, `src/app/landwirtschaft/page.js`, `src/components/Rechner/StromspeicherRechner.js`, `src/components/Foerdercheck/FoerderWizard.js` an.

Dev-Server läuft bereits auf http://localhost:3100 (NICHT neu starten, NICHT `next build` im Projektordner ausführen – das zerschießt den laufenden Server. Für einen Build: `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-verify npx next build`).

## Unternehmen

- **ÖkoInvest GmbH**, Gewerbegebiet 10, 5121 Ostermiething (AT), FN 541505g, LG Ried im Innkreis, eingetragen 10.09.2020. GF: Andreas Wegscheider, Manuel Thaler. Teil der **ÖKOVOLT Gruppe** (seit 2010, Muttergesellschaft ÖKOVOLT GmbH Solartechnik in Türkheim/Bayern; Schwester ÖKOVOLT Solartechnik GmbH in AT). Beteiligungen: GFL – PV-Kraftwerk GmbH (100 %), HIL PV Kraftwerk GmbH (50 %, mit Prime Energy Solutions GmbH). Die Gruppe betreibt eigene Solarparks seit 2012 (z. B. Irsingen, Artern, Tilleda) und hat eigene Rammtechnik (Deutsche Solar & Rammtechnik GmbH).
- Geschäft: Projektentwicklung **Freiflächen-PV, Agri-PV, Solarcarports/Parkplätze, Großspeicher**; Contracting & PPA. Entwickelt **rund 50 MWp pro Jahr neu** (Baureife erst Jahre später – ehrlich kommunizieren).
- Plattform-Ziel: führende Seite im DACH-Raum, Markt durch Digitalisierung erschließen. Einnahmen über **Provision** (Projektbörse: Verkäuferprovision 1,5–3 % nur bei Abschluss; für Investoren und Flächeneigentümer kostenfrei).
- Zielgruppen: Flächeneigentümer, Landwirte (Agri-PV: verpachten / selbst investieren / Investor betreibt + Landwirt ist Mitglied in der Genossenschaft), Investoren (Projekte kaufen, Suchprofil), Projektentwickler/Anbieter (Projekte in die Börse stellen), Unternehmen/Mittelstand (**Reststrom-Pool**: die Firmen, denen die Muttergesellschaft ÖKOVOLT PV + Speicher baut, beziehen den Strom, den sie trotzdem noch kaufen müssen, gebündelt über das virtuelle Kraftwerk von ÖkoInvest → Preise drücken), Kommunen, Bürger (Genossenschaft, Energiegemeinschaften).

## Harte Regeln

1. **Corporate Design nicht zerstören.** Nur die vorhandenen Tokens/Klassen: Farben `ov-*` (Grün, 600 für Buttons), `navy-*`, `ink-*`, `sand-*`, `sun-*` (sparsam). Radien groß (rounded-3xl / rounded-[2rem]). Keine neuen Farben, keine anderen Fonts, keine Emojis im UI.

Keine erfundenen Referenzprojekte, Kunden, Zitate, Auszeichnungen oder Kennzahlen über ÖkoInvest. Belegt nur: siehe „Unternehmen“.
5. **Sprache:** Deutsch, Sie-Form, sachlich-selbstbewusst, keine Werbefloskeln. Echte Umlaute (ä, ö, ü, ß) in allen Texten. Code-Bezeichner und Kommentare deutsch wie im Bestand.

Semantische Überschriften, `aria-*`, Tastaturbedienung, `prefers-reduced-motion` respektieren (globals.css tut das meist schon).
7. **Mobil zuerst prüfen:** Nichts darf bei 360–390 px horizontal überlaufen.

Für Agri-PV, Carports, Karten, Prozesse: **eigene Inline-SVG-Illustrationen** im Markenstil (Grün/Navy/Sand, flach, sauber) statt fremder Bilder.

## Vertrag Formulare / Plattform (wird vom Plattform-Team gebaut)

# Ratgeber-Artikel (inhaltsgetrieben)

Jede Datei in diesem Ordner ist ein Artikel unter `/ratgeber/<slug>`. Die Seite rendert `src/app/ratgeber/[slug]/page.js`. Übersicht, Sitemap, „Weiterlesen“, Inhaltsverzeichnis, Lesezeit und JSON-LD (Article, FAQPage, HowTo, BreadcrumbList) entstehen automatisch.

**Referenz:** `photovoltaik-lohnt-sich.js`

## Neuen Artikel anlegen

1. Datei `src/content/ratgeber/<slug>.js` nach dem Muster unten anlegen. Der Dateiname entspricht dem Slug.
2. `node scripts/ratgeber-index.mjs` ausführen, damit der Artikel registriert wird.
3. Seite im Browser prüfen (Desktop und Handy).

Dateien, die mit `_` beginnen, werden ignoriert (Entwürfe).

## Aufbau

```js
import { ANNAHMEN } from "@/data/solarrechner";   // optional: zentrale Zahlen verwenden

const artikel = {
  slug: "stromspeicher-kosten",                    // = Dateiname, nur a–z, 0–9, Bindestrich

  keywords: ["…", "…"],                            // 5–8 Varianten und Nebenkeywords

  aktualisiert: "2026-09-13",

    { id: "preise", titel: "H2 als Frage oder klare Aussage", tocLabel: "kurz fürs Inhaltsverzeichnis (optional)", bloecke: [ /* siehe Blocktypen */ ] },

};

export default artikel;

### Kategorien (feste Werte)

**Textformatierung** in allen Textfeldern: `**fett**`, `[Linktext](/interner/pfad)` oder `[Linktext](https://extern)`. Kein HTML.

## Redaktionelle Regeln

- **Sie-Form**, sachlich, verständlich, ohne Werbesprech. Stand-Datum nennen, wenn Zahlen sich ändern.

Belegt sind: Fachbetrieb in Türkheim, über 15 Jahre Erfahrung, Planung/Montage/Anmeldung aus einer Hand, Partner von Sigenergy, Fronius, Huawei, Solis, meteocontrol und BYD (Freigabe für deren Marketing- und Produktfotos; Bildquellen in `public/Images/Ratgeber/QUELLEN.md` dokumentieren).

- **Umfang:** 1.500–3.000 Wörter Inhalt. Tiefe vor Länge – nichts aufblähen.

Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.

- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding § 42c EnWG and Energy Sharing:

## Key Timeline and Implementation

§ 42c EnWG entered into force on 22 December 2025. The obligation for distribution system operators to implement it technically takes effect on 1 June 2026.

## Geographic Scope - Expansion to Adjacent Grid Areas

Regarding the expansion to adjacent grid areas in 2028: Initially, all participating units must be located within the same balancing area of a distribution system operator. As of 1 June 2028, the geographical scope will be expanded, allowing contracts between actors in directly adjacent balancing areas within the same control zone. # § 42c EnWG - Zusammenfassung Absätze 1-3

## Anlagenbetreiber (Absatz 1, Nr. 1)
Betreiber darf sein: "natürliche Person oder rechtsfähige Personengesellschaft oder juristische Person des Privatrechts", wobei alle Gesellschafter/Mitglieder selbst Letztverbraucher oder juristische Personen des öffentlichen Rechts sein müssen.

**Ausschluss:** Juristische Personen des öffentlichen Rechts dürfen nicht selbst Betreiber sein, sondern nur als Gesellschafter/Mitglieder fungieren. Genossenschaften sind nicht explizit genannt.

## Zulässige Anlagen (Absatz 1, Satz 1)
- Stromerzeugungsanlagen aus erneuerbaren Energien
- Energiespeicheranlagen, die ausschließlich erneuerbare Elektrizität zwischenspeichern

## KMU-Definition (Absatz 2)
Unternehmen gelten nur als Letztverbraucher, wenn sie "Kleinstunternehmen, kleine oder mittlere Unternehmen" nach EU-Empfehlung 2003/361/EG sind.

## Vollversorgungspflicht
Die §§ 5, 40-42 entfallen bei kleineren Anlagen (Absatz 7). Das bedeutet: **Keine umfassenden Lieferantenpflichten** bei max. 30 kW (Haushalte) oder 100 kW (Mehrparteienhäuser).

# Energy Sharing under § 42c EnWG: Summary

**Eligible Participants:**
Natural persons, legal partnerships, and private-law entities can participate, provided they operate renewable plants not primarily for commercial purposes. SMEs qualify, including municipal ones. Plant operators cannot share electricity with themselves.

**Grid Fee Reductions:**
None exist. The document states that "taxes, levies, surcharges, and grid charges apply fully to shared electricity," making the arrangement economically challenging compared to other EU countries.

**Supplier Obligations Relief:**
Household customers receive limited exemptions. The text notes they're exempt from "notification requirement under Section 5 EnWG and obligations related to invoice design and electricity labelling." However, cooperatively organized arrangements retain full supplier obligations.

**Smart Meter Requirement:**
Accounting requires "15‑minute intervals to allow precise allocation of generation and consumption," though the document doesn't explicitly mandate smart meters.

**Start Date:**
Implementation begins June 1, 2026, initially within single balancing areas, expanding to adjacent areas by June 1, 2028.

**Criticisms:**
The whitepaper identifies significant gaps: unresolved metering processes, unclear data access rights, geographical limitations, and absent financial incentives undermine feasibility. It concludes energy sharing is "legally possible, but technically, organizationally, and economically only partially feasible."

**Bundesnetzagentur Mention:**
No reference to Bundesnetzagentur determinations appears in this content.

# Zusammenfassung: Energiegemeinschaften nach österreichischem ElWG

## Modelle
Das ElWG definiert folgende Modelle der gemeinsamen Energienutzung:
- **EEG** (Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften)
- **BEG** (Bürgerenergiegemeinschaften)
- **P2P** (Peer-to-Peer-Verträge)
- **EVA** (Eigenversorgungsanlage)
- **GEA** (Gemeinschaftliche Erzeugungsanlagen)

## Netzentgeltreduktionen
Die konkrete Höhe wird durch die Systemnutzungsentgelt-Verordnung (SNE-VO) ab 01.01.2027 festgelegt. Vergünstigungen gelten für:
- **Zonelevel 1-5**: "Reduktion bei Netzentgelten" in Standort-, Lokal- und Regionalbereich
- **Zonelevel 6-7**: Keine Vergünstigungen (österreichweite Gebotszone)

Bis Ende 2026 erhalten nur EEG-Mitglieder reduzierte Netzarbeitstarife.

## Entfall Abgaben
Der Entfall von Elektrizitätsabgabe und Erneuerbaren-Förderbeitrag "betrifft weiterhin ausschließlich Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften" (§ 68 Abs. 3-4 ElWG).

## Mehrfachteilnahme
Die Website enthält einen Verweis auf Details zur Mehrfachteilnahme, konkrete Zahlen sind aber nicht angegeben.

## Teilnehmerkreis
- Aktive Kunden (Standard)
- Große Unternehmen: dürfen an BEG und P2P teilnehmen, **nicht** an EEG
- Leistungsgrenze für Erzeugungsanlagen: **6 MW**

## Österreichweite Umsetzung
BEG, P2P und EVA können ab 01.04.2027 österreichweit umgesetzt werden.

## Relevante Paragraphen
§ 65-72 ElWG regeln die Bürgerenergie-Bestimmungen.

## Key Information about LEG and Netznutzungsentgelt Reduction

Since January 2026, it is possible to market locally generated electricity via the public grid within a district or municipality through a "local electricity community" (LEG).

### Netznutzungsentgelt Reduction Rates

For a LEG, there is a reduction on the network usage fee (40% within network level 7 and 20% within network level 5). This is one of the key advantages of participating in a LEG, as for electricity flowing within the community, the network fee is reduced by up to 40 percent.

### Regulatory Framework

The new regulations - including those for local electricity communities - came into force on January 1, 2026. The specific regulations are governed by the Stromversorgungsverordnung (StromVV) and related legislation from the Bundesamt für Energie (BFE).

The reduction percentage depends on the network topology: participants connected to network level 7 (NE7) receive a 40% reduction, while those at network level 5 (NE5) receive a 20% reduction on their network usage fees.

## Overview

The Mehrfachteilnahme (multiple participation) enables active customers to simultaneously participate in up to five different citizen energy models (Energiegemeinschaften, Peer-to-Peer contract communities, joint generation facilities or self-supply facilities).

## Key Details

**Legal Framework:** The new regulations for shared energy use and Energiegemeinschaften (Citizen Energy – ElWG § 65 Abs. 1 Z 6 and Abs. 2 as well as §§ 66 to 72) come into force on 01.10.2026.

**Participation Factor:** The participation factor indicates the percentage of generation/consumption (according to measurement) with which the metering point participates in the energy community. For the metering point, the sum of individual participations may not exceed 100 percent and must be at least 1 percent.

"Haushalte und Betriebe in einem Quartier oder einer Gemeinde können in einer LEG den selbst produzierten Strom gemeinsam nutzen und über das öffentliche Netz miteinander teilen."

**Tariff Benefit:**
"Die LEG profitiert von einem günstigeren Netztarif."

**Limitations in Article:**
The article does not provide specific information regarding:
- Exact prerequisites for forming a LEG
- Netzbetreiber (grid operator) requirements
- Netzebene (network level) specifications
- Mindestproduktionsleistung (minimum production capacity)

The article mentions these regulations are part of implementing federal law on secure power supply and are documented in the Energieverordnung (EnV) and Stromversorgungsverordnung (StromVV), but detailed technical specifications are not included in this overview article. You would need to consult those specific ordinances for comprehensive details.

# Lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaft (LEG) Summary

Based on the Wikipedia article, here's what you need to know about LEG in Switzerland:

## What is LEG?

A "Lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaft" is a Swiss model where "locally produced electricity is sold locally within the municipality via the local power grid." Unlike virtual arrangements (vZEV), LEG participants aren't restricted to a single connection point, though network fees still apply.

## Key Requirements

Participants must meet several criteria:
- **Generation capacity**: At least 5% of consumers' total connection capacity
- **Geographic scope**: All members must connect through the same grid operator at identical voltage levels
- **Smart meters**: All connection points require intelligent metering systems
- **Representation**: A designated LEG representative acts as the network operator's contact
- **Voluntary participation**: Membership is optional for consumers and producers

## Financial Benefits

Members negotiate internal energy pricing. "The grid network usage involves a reduced rate," with the Federal Council defining maximum discounts of up to 60%, depending on grid topology.

## Implementation Timeline

LEG regulations begin January 1, 2026, following the first phase of electricity law reforms (January 1, 2025). Registration requires three months, during which smart meters must be installed.

## Negative Strompreise und Marktprämie

Seit Februar 2025 gilt das Solarspitzengesetz: Bei negativen Preisen entfällt für Neuanlagen die Marktprämie ab der ersten Viertelstunde. ## Direktvermarktung unter 100 kW

Das Solarspitzengesetz 2025 erleichtert die Direktvermarktung von Solarstrom erheblich, insbesondere für kleinere PV-Anlagen. Für Anlagen unter 100 kW werden die bürokratischen Hürden deutlich reduziert. Die Direktvermarktung für Anlagen unter 100 kWp wird deutlich vereinfacht.

Neue PV-Anlagen ab 7 kWp müssen mit einem Smart Meter mit daran gekoppelter Steuereinrichtung ausgestattet werden. # Fernsteuerbarkeit bei Direktvermarktung nach § 10b EEG 2023

## Welche Anlagen müssen fernsteuerbar sein?

Anlagen mit **mehr als 25 Kilowatt installierter Leistung**, die Strom direkt vermarkten, müssen die Anforderungen erfüllen.

## Was bedeutet "fernsteuerbar"?

Die Betreiber müssen ihre Anlagen mit Einrichtungen ausstatten, durch die das Direktvermarktungsunternehmen oder der Stromkäufer:

1. **Abrufbarkeit**: "jederzeit die Ist-Einspeisung abrufen kann"

2. **Fernregelung**: "die Einspeiseleistung vollständig oder...stufenweise oder stufenlos ferngesteuert regeln kann"

Die Regelung muss in dem Umfang erfolgen, "der für eine bedarfsgerechte Einspeisung des Stroms erforderlich" ist.

## Rolle des Smart-Meter-Gateways

Ab **1. Januar 2028** und nach Einbau eines intelligenten Messsystems können die Anforderungen über das Smart-Meter-Gateway erfüllt werden. Bis dahin oder alternativ müssen Betreiber Übertragungstechniken verwenden, die "dem Stand der Technik bei Inbetriebnahme der Anlage entsprechen und wirtschaftlich vertretbar sind".

Die Einhaltung wird vermutet, wenn Standards des Bundesamtes für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik beachtet werden.

# Solarspitzengesetz: Kernpunkte

**Negative Preise ohne Vergütung:**
Ab Inkrafttreten des Gesetzes werden neue PV-Anlagen bei negativen Strompreisen nicht vergütet. Die Förderung wird auf einen späteren Zeitpunkt verschoben – künftig bereits für einzelne Viertelstunden. Kleine Anlagen unter 2 kWp sind ausgenommen, bis die Bundesnetzagentur anders entscheidet.

**Verlängerung Förderzeitraum:**
Die entgangene Vergütung wird nach Ablauf der 20-jährigen Förderung nachgeholt, unter Berücksichtigung des solaren Ertragspotenzials der betreffenden Monate.

**Einspeisebegrenzung 60% ohne Smart Meter:**
Neue Anlagen unter 25 kW müssen die Einspeiseleistung auf 60 Prozent begrenzen – aber nur bis ein intelligentes Messsystem und Steuerungseinrichtung eingebaut sind.

**Direktvermarktungsgrenze:**
Anlagen zwischen 25–100 kW in freiwilliger Direktvermarktung müssen fernsteuerbar sein. Mit Speichern entstehen „nahezu keine Nachteile" durch intelligente Zwischenspeicherung.

**Steuerbarkeit:**
Anlagenbetreiber müssen Anforderungen zur Fernsteuerbarkeit erfüllen; Verstoß kann zur Netzabschaltung führen – mit einstündiger Frist zur Behebung.

Based on the search results, here is relevant information about Direktvermarktung (direct marketing) and the Marktprämienmodell (market premium model) for EEG renewable energy plants:

## Key Statistics from 2023 Monitoring Report

The share of EEG market premiums amounted to 75 percent of all EEG payments in 2023. Additionally, direct marketing other than market premiums rose to a share of just under 11 percent.

## How the Market Premium Model Works

The market premium is an EEG-funded payment to operators of renewable energy plants who receive no fixed EEG compensation but participate in direct marketing, and is paid by the distribution network operator to equalize the difference between the current market value and the plant-specific subsidy level.

The height of individual funding is determined through a bidding procedure by the Bundesnetzagentur for onshore wind energy, solar plants, biomass plants and offshore wind energy plants.

## Growth in Direct Marketing

Since the introduction of the market premium model, the share of plants that directly market their power in this way has grown steadily and powerfully.

The search results contain comprehensive information about the market premium model from the Bundesnetzagentur's official 2024 monitoring report, though specific details about the number of direct marketers weren't included in these particular results.

## Stromsteuer-Gesetzgebung ab 1. Januar 2026

The law permanently reduces the electricity tax for manufacturing companies and agriculture/forestry businesses to the EU minimum tax rate of 0.05 cents per kilowatt-hour starting with a minimum annual consumption of 12.5 megawatt-hours.

The German Bundestag passed the Third Law to Amend the Energy Tax and Electricity Tax Act (Bundestag document 21/1866) on November 13, 2025, which takes effect on January 1, 2026.

### Key Details:

- **Beneficiaries**: Approximately 600,000 companies, including the majority of skilled trades, will benefit
- **Entlastung**: Eligible businesses receive a refund of 2.00 ct/kWh (previously only 0.513 ct/kWh) with a minimum consumption of 12,500 kWh
- **Financial Impact**: The government has budgeted loss of revenue of 1.5 billion euros for 2026, with approximately 3 billion euros annually from 2027 onward
- **Scope**: Manufacturing includes mining, automotive, machinery, chemicals, energy and water supply, and construction, while agriculture and forestry includes farming, forestry operations, and fish farming

Ich habe die Suchergebnisse für Ihre Anfrage zum vZEV (virtueller Zusammenschluss zum Eigenverbrauch) 2025 zusammengefasst:

## Schlüsselinformationen zum vZEV

**Neuerung seit 2025:**
Seit dem 1. Januar 2025 gibt es die Möglichkeit, einen virtuellen Zusammenschluss zum Eigenverbrauch (vZEV) zu bilden.

**Anschlussleitungen und Netzbetreiber:**
Seit dem 1. Januar 2025 dürfen neu auch Anschlussleitungen sowie die Infrastruktur bei Netzanschlusspunkten für den Eigenverbrauch genutzt werden. Beim virtuellen ZEV dürfen die Anschlussleitungen des Verteilnetzbetreibers zum öffentlichen Stromnetz genutzt werden, um den Strom unter den verschiedenen vZEV-Teilnehmern zu verteilen.

**10-Prozent-Anforderung:**
Die gesamte Produktionsleistung muss mindestens 10 Prozent der gesamten Anschlussleistung des Zusammenschlusses betragen.

**Voraussetzungen:**
Mieterinnen und Eigentümer von benachbarten Liegenschaften können einem vZEV beitreten, wenn sie am gleichen Netzanschlusspunkt angeschlossen sind. Für die Messung in einem vZEV ist es Pflicht, dass Smart Meter (Stromzähler) installiert sind.

**Messpunkte:**
Die Messdaten der verschiedenen Zähler werden virtuell zusammengefasst und die gemeinsamen Teilnehmer am vZEV müssen vom Netzbetreiber wie ein einziger Endverbraucher behandelt werden.

Die Suchergebnisse zeigen, dass verschiedene Schweizer Netzbetreiber (EWB, Regio Energie, BKW und andere) bereits Leitfäden und Informationen zum vZEV bereitstellen.

Based on the search results, here's information about the Bundesnetzagentur regulations on controllable consumption devices under § 14a EnWG, Modul 3, and time-variable network fees for 2025:

## Modul 3 - Time-Variable Network Fees

As of April 2025, network operators must offer consumers time-variable network fees in the form of Module 3. Module 3 can only be selected in combination with Module 1.

## Structure of Module 3

The model provides multiple time windows with three price levels of the locally applicable network fees (HT / NT / ST). The time windows and price levels are set on a calendar-year basis, apply to the entire network area, and must be settled in at least two quarters of a year.

## Implementation Timeline

Module 3 must be settled by network operators starting April 1, 2025, because digitalization in low-voltage networks must advance further.

## Transparency and Billing

Power suppliers are obligated to transparently show the network fee and its reduction on the consumer billing statement. The existing structure of the electricity supply contract is to be used for settlement of the reduced fees. The power supplier is obligated to transparently show the modules used on the consumer bill. No new billing relationship between end consumer and network operator is created.

## Ordering Process

It has been shown that ordering Module 3 proceeds faster in market communication processes when the order is placed with the supplier in cases where a contractual relationship already exists between the operator of a controllable consumption device and the power supplier.

**Deutschland:** Energy Sharing nach § 42c EnWG gilt seit dem **1. Juni 2026** innerhalb des Bilanzierungsgebiets eines Verteilnetzbetreibers, ab dem **1. Juni 2028** auch im direkt angrenzenden Gebiet derselben Regelzone. Netzentgelte, Umlagen und Steuern fallen auf geteilten Strom in voller Höhe an.
**Österreich:** Rund **500.000 Zählpunkte** nehmen laut Koordinationsstelle an über 12.000 Modellen der gemeinsamen Energienutzung teil (Stand September 2026). Lokale Erneuerbare-Energie-Gemeinschaften sparen bisher 57 % des Netznutzungs-Arbeitspreises; mit dem ElWG gelten ab 1. Oktober 2026 neue Regeln.
**Schweiz:** Seit 1. Januar 2026 gibt es die **lokale Elektrizitätsgemeinschaft (LEG)** innerhalb einer Gemeinde – mit 40 % Abschlag auf den Netznutzungstarif (20 % bei mehreren Netzebenen). ZEV und vZEV bleiben die Lösung am Gebäude bzw. Netzanschlusspunkt.
**Keine Gemeinschaft deckt den ganzen Bedarf.** Den Reststrom beziehen alle Teilnehmer weiterhin von einem Lieferanten ihrer Wahl – dort liegt für Unternehmen oft der größere Hebel.

virtuelles-kraftwerk 2086 Wörter 10 Min title 60 seo 57 desc 163
**Ein virtuelles Kraftwerk (VKW) verbindet viele dezentrale Anlagen – Solarparks, Wind, Speicher, flexible Verbraucher – über eine Leitwarte und Fernsteuerung zu einem Verbund**, der am Strommarkt auftritt wie ein großes Kraftwerk.
Neue Erneuerbaren-Anlagen ab **100 kW** müssen ihren Strom in der Regel direkt vermarkten und sind in **Redispatch 2.0** eingebunden. Das VKW übernimmt Prognose, Fahrplan, Fernsteuerung und Datenmeldungen.
Geld verdient wird am **Day-Ahead- und Intraday-Markt**, mit **Regelenergie** (Mindestgebot meist 1 MW – nur im Pool für kleine Einheiten erreichbar) und durch das Verschieben von Strom mit Speichern und flexiblen Lasten.
Für Unternehmen senkt der Verbund die Beschaffungskosten: Im Beispiel dieses Artikels spart ein Betrieb mit 800 MWh Verbrauch und neuer PV rund **3.700 € bis 13.900 € im Jahr** beim Reststrom – Orientierung, kein Angebot.

- Title: "Energy Sharing und Energiegemeinschaften: DE, AT und CH im Vergleich" (68 characters). seoTitle 55, description 160 characters.
- Length: 2,434 words, shown as 12 min reading time. 14 internal links in the body.
- Image: `/img/gewerbedach.jpg`. Alt text: technician with a radio on a flat roof with solar modules, houses and industrial halls behind.
- Contents: kurzFazit; Germany (§ 42c EnWG); Austria (EEG/BEG/GEA, the new ElWG law, table of grid-fee discounts); Switzerland (ZEV/vZEV/LEG); a large DE/AT/CH comparison table; a worked example for a small business in Germany built on `STROM.bestandteile`; limits; steps (`ablauf`); tool block → `/rechner/reststrom`; 7 FAQs. Uses `GEMEINSCHAFTEN` from `markt.js`.
- Research findings:
  - § 42c EnWG came into force on 22.12.2025.
  - Grid operators must enable sharing from 1.6.2026 within one balancing area. From 1.6.2028 it extends to directly adjacent balancing areas in the same control zone.
  - Size limits are 30 kW for households and 100 kW for multi-party buildings.
  - Only SMEs may be buyers. Measurement must be quarter-hourly.
  - Grid fees and levies apply in full to shared power.
  - A Bürgerenergiegesellschaft under § 3 Nr. 15 EEG needs at least 50 natural persons, 75 % of votes held within 50 km, and no member above 10 %.
